title: Kodak launches Slice touchscreen camera
summary: Kodak has launched the Slice touchscreen camera, an attempt to compete with other manufacturers offering similar interfaces. The 14MP camera features a 3.5-inch touchscreen, 720p 30 FPS video, and can store up to 5,000 pictures with a search feature. It will retail for $349.95 MSRP starting in April 2010 and will be available through Best Buy, Amazon.com, and Kodak.com.

title: Amazon's Kindle DX goes international
summary: Amazon's Kindle DX model, featuring a screen 2.5 times larger than the international Kindle, has been made available in over 100 countries. The device, priced at $489, is designed for highly-formatted content like magazines and textbooks, with shipments beginning on January 19. Amazon founder Jeff Bezos envisions a future where "every book ever printed" is available on Kindle.

title: Understanding cloud computing pricing
summary: This article discusses the complexities of cloud computing pricing models, highlighting how providers base charges on various factors like storage, CPU time, and traffic. It compares pricing structures and services from providers like GoGrid, Rackspace, and Amazon, emphasizing the need for IT managers to carefully negotiate and understand all costs. The piece concludes by noting the ongoing challenges for cloud providers in simplifying pricing and ensuring service level agreements (SLAs).

title: P&G to sell directly to customers on Web site
summary: Procter & Gamble is launching an "eStore" to sell hundreds of its products directly to consumers online, which will initially offer flat-rate shipping. While P&G states the eStore is primarily a consumer research "lab" to gather data on online shopping behavior, it could place the company in direct competition with its traditional retailers. P&G aims to use this platform to understand consumer responses to digital ads, coupons, and promotions.

title: P&G floats selling products on its own website
summary: Procter & Gamble is launching its own "eStore" this month to sell products directly to consumers, aiming to significantly increase online sales which accounted for only 0.6% of its 2009 revenue. The eStore, operated by PFSweb Inc., will initially cater to U.S. shoppers and will serve as a "learning lab" to gather data on online purchasing habits, while also improving relationships with existing online retailers like Wal-Mart and Amazon. This move signifies P&G's first broad online retail strategy, acknowledging the overdue trend for consumer packaged goods companies to establish an online presence.

title: Apple's tablet could change e-book world
summary: Apple Inc. is poised to potentially disrupt the e-book reader market with its upcoming tablet device, despite CEO Steve Jobs' previous skepticism about e-readers. Industry observers believe the tablet, set to be unveiled, could redefine digital reading much like the iPod did for music. This move could challenge Amazon's Kindle dominance and introduce a new major player into the e-book publishing landscape, particularly if Apple establishes its own online bookstore.

title: Apple unveils iPad tablet computer
summary: Apple Inc. unveiled its iPad tablet computer, priced starting at $499, significantly below analyst expectations. CEO Steve Jobs presented the device, highlighting its 9.7-inch touch screen, 10-hour battery life, and connectivity options, including Wi-Fi and AT&T 3G plans. The iPad is positioned as a competitor to e-book readers like Amazon's Kindle and aims to create a new category of devices by blending laptop and smartphone capabilities, with potential major implications for the gaming industry.

title: Apple introduces iPad tablet
summary: Apple Inc. unveiled its new tablet-style iPad, starting at $499, a price significantly lower than anticipated by some analysts. CEO Steve Jobs described the device as more intimate than a laptop and more capable than a smartphone, highlighting its 9.7-inch touch screen, long battery life, and connectivity options. The iPad aims to compete with e-book readers like Amazon's Kindle and offers a new platform for gaming and video, with Apple expecting a "gold rush" for developers creating new applications.

title: Apple unveils the 'magical' iPad
summary: Apple CEO Steve Jobs unveiled the highly anticipated iPad tablet, calling it a "magical and revolutionary product." The device features a 10-inch touchscreen, runs existing Apple apps, and is available in various storage capacities, with prices starting at $499. The iPad is also expected to compete with e-readers, offering a new iBook interface.
